newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals firm on dollar decline.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals firm on dollar decline.

text.p: Regional currencies were mostly firmer on Thursday following the dollar's overnight decline and softened tone against major currencies.

The dollar came under pressure along with U.S. stocks and bonds on growing nervousness that Wall Street might be reaching the end of its record-breaking streak. Renewed fears of a Japanese rate hike also weighed on the U.S. unit on Thursday.
Dealers said thin year-end conditions exaggerated moves in forex markets as stop-loss orders were easily triggered.
"If you enter the market with $50-$60 (million) in a normal market the rate would move 10 points. But now, it could be 50 to 60 points," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.
He noted that the dollar's movements were likely to dominate activity in regional currencies, and players should look to buy the dollar on any dips as its tone remained positive.
In Indonesia, the rupiah's upside was restricted by expectations of a higher central bank fixing in the afternoon.
But Jakarta dealers said short-term swaps rose on overseas buying, possibly driven by speculation or short-covering ahead of the weekend.
"Singapore buying pushed the short-term swaps up briefly minutes after the open, but the spot rate barely moved," said a European bank dealer said.
Another foreign bank dealer said the market appeared to have slowed down ahead of the year-end and investors were only working to maintain profits.
Dealers said the spot rate was trapped in a narrow range on the back of sufficient rupiah liquidity following the central bank's injection of 644 billion rupiah.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,352.50/53.00 at 0445 GMT against an opening of 2,352.50/53.25.
Dealers said they expected the central bank to raise its intervention and conversion bands later on Thursday following increases on Monday and Tuesday.
The central bank has maintained a three-to-four-point rupiah depreciation a week since late September.

The Thai baht rose to 25.540-25.543 at 0445 GMT against 25.549-25.554 late on Wednesday in line with the weakened dollar/majors. The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.51 from 25.54 on Wednesday.
"Dollar/baht is trading on the higher end of the band. The market is still kind of skeptical about the policies announced yesterday," said a Singapore dealer.
"Buying of dollars is favoured on any kind of dip to the lower end of the band," he added.
The new Thai government said on Wednesday that it aimed to curb the widening current account deficit by reducing spending and boosting revenues.
It also said it planned to deregulate the financial sector in stages and further develop money and capital markets.
The Malaysian ringgit was firmer but dealers said strong gains would be blocked by local demand for dollars around 2.5170/80 ringgit.
Dealers said selling of the dollar started around 2.5205 but some short-covering was limiting the dollar/ringgit downside.
"The ringgit's rise was mainly due to dollar/majors decline. There's really not much demand for ringgit," said a local bank dealer. He expects a 40-point trading range for the day.
Further south, the Singapore dollar breached the 1.4000 psychological level against its U.S. counterpart on the back of the U.S. dollar's weakness.
Dealers said dollar/Sing would be picked up near the 1.3970 level but a series of sell orders were expected above 1.4000.
They said the Monetary Authority of Singapore was not expected to intervene as the Singapore dollar's rise was in line with the U.S. unit's drop.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
